title: Cohomology of the affine tensor test by an inverse-image base skyscraper
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $f:U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ its scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], and $M^\bullet$ an arbitrary complex of $A$-modules. Put $\mathcal B=f^{-1}\mathcal O_V$ and $C^\bullet=\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal B}\widetilde{M^\bullet}$ along the canonical structure map [def-pc-module-pullback, lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence]. For $x=\mathfrak q\in U$, put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$ and $s=f(x)$. Let $L$ be any $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module and $\mathcal G=i_{s,*}L$ the ringed-module skyscraper on $V$ using the affine germ isomorphism $\mathcal O_{V,s}\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization, def-pc-ringed-module-skyscraper]. For every integer $i$, the derived comparison of [lem-trf-affine-relative-stalk-resolution-iso] induces an isomorphism of $R_{\mathfrak p}$-modules
$$\bigl(H^i(QC^\bullet\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal B}f^{-1}\mathcal G)\bigr)_x\cong H^i(Q(M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q})\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_{\mathfrak p}}L).$$
The left side is the actual module stalk with scalars transported along the isomorphism $e_x:R_{\mathfrak p}\cong\mathcal B_x$ of [lem-trf-affine-relative-stalk-resolution-iso] [def-pc-module-stalk-functor], the localization $M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}$ is termwise [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and both derived tensors are computed by K-flat resolutions [def-trf-ringed-complex-derived-tensor-vanishing, def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. There are no boundedness or finiteness hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 0DHY, lemma-tor-dimension-rel-affine, stalk argument; cohomology consequence of the derived inverse-image base-skyscraper tensor comparison.

proof.text: Put $K=QC^\bullet\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal B}f^{-1}\mathcal G$, and use exactly the functor $S_x$ of [lem-trf-affine-relative-stalk-resolution-iso], including its restriction of scalars along $e_x$. That statement supplies its exactness and its induced functor on derived categories. For any complex $T^\bullet$ representing $K$, exactness gives $S_x(\ker d^i)=\ker(S_xd^i)$, $S_x(\operatorname{im}d^{i-1})=\operatorname{im}(S_xd^{i-1})$, and preserves their quotient. Thus $S_xH^i(K)\cong H^i(S_xK)$, naturally in $K$, by the formula $H^i=\ker d^i/\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$. These identifications also show that termwise $S_x$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so the calculation is independent of the representative. Its left side is precisely the actual stalk $(H^i(K))_x$ with the stipulated $R_{\mathfrak p}$-action.

source.place: Tag 09U9, lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk, proof: exact stalks commute with cohomology; with the affine identifications of Tag 0DHY, lemma-tor-dimension-rel-affine in perfect.tex.

proof.text: Apply the skyscraper specialization in [lem-trf-affine-relative-stalk-resolution-iso] with the given $R\to A$, $M^\bullet$, $x=\mathfrak q$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$ and arbitrary $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $L$. It gives $\beta:S_xK\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(M^\bullet_{\mathfrak q})\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_{\mathfrak p}}L$ in $D(R_{\mathfrak p})$, for the very skyscraper and K-flat derived tensors in the statement. Apply the cohomology functor $H^i$ to $\beta$ and its inverse; their composites are identities because functors preserve composition and identities. Compose the resulting isomorphism with Step 1. This is the required isomorphism induced by the derived comparison. All maps are $R_{\mathfrak p}$-linear, since both $S_x$ and $H^i$ take values with those scalars, and Step 1 used the same $e_x$. The kernel/image/quotient computation uses only degrees $i-1,i,i+1$, so it applies to every integer $i$ and unbounded complexes without further hypotheses.
